United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP GetConfiguration Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. When parsing GetConfiguration requests, the process does not properly validate the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28968.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP backend configuration requests. The issue results from the lack of authentication prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29063.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP Backend Configuration Hard-Coded Credentials Authentication Bypass Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to bypass authentication on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the configuration of the OCPP backend settings interface. The issue results from the use of hard-coded credentials. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute arbitrary code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29056.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A FTP URL Path Parsing Stack-based Buffer Overflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of FTP URL paths during firmware updates. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28960.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A OCPP UpdateFirmware Out-Of-Bounds Write Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP UpdateFirmware requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of user-supplied data, which can result in a write past the end of an allocated buffer. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-29487.

A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin. Insufficient sanitization of data passed to queries against the external database allows an authenticated user with course editing permissions to perform a Structured Query Language (SQL) injection attack. When this non-default plugin is enabled, an attacker can exploit this issue to view, modify, or delete sensitive records within the connected external database.

Stoatchat before 0.16.5 contains an unbounded JXL image decoding vulnerability in revolt_files decode_image that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory via the january /proxy endpoint. Attackers can request a small hosted JXL file declaring 12000x12000 pixels through /proxy to trigger huge allocations, OOM-killing january and denying proxy and embed service.

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows space admins to reach internal hosts because Nextcloud.get_client builds WebDAV clients from Storage.url without calling safe_request. Attackers can create a NEXTCLOUD storage via POST /api/storage/ pointing at internal hosts, import a file, then call GET /api/get_recipe_file/<id>/ to read internal service or cloud metadata responses.

parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, DependencyGraph.tree and DependencyGraph.triples walk parsed dependency edges through unbounded Python recursion and do not use a working cycle or depth guard. A crafted CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency file containing a sufficiently long chain can raise RecursionError when the documented traversal APIs are called, aborting the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it takes every upgraded socket and dispatches the request through the Fastify router before the WebSocket library takes ownership of the socket. Node.js removes its own error listener from the socket before emitting the upgrade event, and the plugin does not attach one of its own during routing, so a socket error such as a client connection reset that arrives before the WebSocket library takes over is unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. The error window is open whenever anything asynchronous runs between dispatch and the route handler, such as an async hook on the proxied route or any unrelated async route in the application. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by a connection reset is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.4.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade request whose path carries a URL fragment is matched by the router and answered with a successful upgrade before the upstream link is created. Building the upstream target then throws, the error is only logged, and the accepted client socket is left open with no error listener, so the next frame the client sends becomes an unhandled error and terminates the Node.js process. A request target that is not a valid URL reference reaching a parameterized prefix triggers the same path. A single unauthenticated upgrade request followed by one frame is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

RepoManager is a self-hosted deb/rpm package repository. Prior to 5.13.3, an attacker who controls an upstream RPM repository mirrored by a RepoManager instance can provide a package filename through the primary.xml <location href> field; the mirror passes that filename into a shell-interpreted RPM query, allowing shell metacharacters to execute commands as the www-data service account. The target must mirror an upstream repository controlled by the attacker, and the default "Check GPG signatures" option triggers the vulnerable call. The command executes before a later signature-verification failure, so a valid signed package is not required. Fixed in 5.13.3.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 9.0.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, a WebSocket upgrade that is pipelined behind another HTTP request on the same cleartext connection arrives while that request's response is still attached to the socket. The shared upgrade listener sees the socket is already claimed and returns early without taking the upgrade, but it does not attach an error listener to the raw socket, and Node.js has already removed its own error listener before emitting the upgrade event. A later socket error on that connection, such as a client connection reset, is therefore unhandled and terminates the Node.js process. A single unauthenticated connection that pipelines an upgrade behind a normal request and then resets is enough to crash the server, and it can be repeated to keep the process down. Upgrades over TLS are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

Go-Guerrilla SMTP Daemon is a lightweight SMTP server written in Go. In 1.6.7 and earlier, according to the repository advisory's structured affected range, server.go defines the seven-byte cmdXCLIENT token, but the XCLIENT handler slices input[8:] after matching only that seven-byte verb, so a bare command causes an out-of-bounds panic in handleClient and terminates the daemon because that connection goroutine does not recover the panic. The issue is reachable by an unauthenticated client when the non-default xclient_on setting is enabled; no HELO command is required. The repository fix is present in version 1.6.7-1.

aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.12.1, the QoS 2 transaction handler in amqtt/mqtt/protocol/handler.py, _handle_qos2_message_flow(), can retain transaction state and packet identifiers when a client disconnects before the handshake completes, unlike QoS 1 flows that expire after the default five-second timeout. A remote client can repeatedly begin QoS 2 flows and disconnect without maintaining long-lived connections; anonymous clients can do this with the default configuration, while authenticated deployments remain affected when a client may initiate QoS 2 flows. The retained state grows broker memory until resource exhaustion can terminate the process; no confidentiality or integrity impact is identified. This issue is fixed in version 0.12.1.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could create and share a metric alert that causes Analytics Workspace to run a malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) when another authenticated user opens a link to the alert. The malicious SPL could expose data, modify data, or disrupt services available in the affected session. 
The vulnerability is possible because Analytics Workspace does not fully neutralize metric alert names before including the names in SPL.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the user by tricking them into opening a link that the attacker creates. The user who holds the "power" Splunk role should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Alerts in the Analytics Workspace (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/analytics-workspace/10.4/using-the-analytics-workspace/alerts-in-the-analytics-workspace) and Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could craft a shared Classic Dashboard that runs arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands for another authenticated user. Exploitation requires the dashboard viewer to open the shared dashboard. The injected commands could access data available to the dashboard viewer, modify data available to the dashboard viewer, and partially disrupt Splunk Enterprise.
For more information see Add sparklines to search results (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.6/calculate-statistics/add-sparklines-to-search-results), Configure dashboard permissions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/simple-xml-dashboards/10.6/manage-and-share-dashboards/configure-dashboard-permissions), and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could add attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) to a shared dashboard. When another user opens the dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise could run the attacker-controlled SPL using the permissions of that dashboard viewer. The attacker-controlled SPL could expose stored credentials, modify indexed data, and reduce availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize special elements in search filter values before it builds optimized search jobs.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared dashboard. The malicious SPL could run using the permissions of the user who opened the dashboard and could access or modify data available to that user and disrupt Splunk Enterprise availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not preserve quoted search argument boundaries when it processes a dashboard search.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role, should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could access RapidDiag process metadata and log file inventory information through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because certain RapidDiag REST API endpoints accept a factory-default shared key for node authentication, which lets requests bypass Splunk user authentication.
For more information see Using RapidDiag (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/troubleshoot/9.0/contact-splunk-support/using-rapiddiag) and Secure Splunk Enterprise services with pass4SymmKey (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.0/secure-distributed-and-clustered-splunk-environments/secure-splunk-enterprise-services-with-pass4symmkey) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user could access live event data from the indexing pipeline through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API on a standalone instance or a search head that is not an indexer cluster member.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise accepts an empty shared key during service authentication.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, an unauthenticated user who can connect to a Splunk-to-Splunk (S2S) data forwarding receiver could cause the Splunk daemon to terminate unexpectedly. The unexpected termination interrupts data indexing and access to the management API and Splunk Web until the Splunk Enterprise process restarts.
The vulnerability is possible because the S2S data forwarding receiver does not validate an optional field in forwarded event data, which results in a null pointer dereference when the field is missing.
For more information see Intermediate data routing using universal and heavy forwarders (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/get-started/splunk-validated-architectures/getting-data-in-forwarding-and-preprocessing/intermediate-data-routing-using-universal-and-heavy-forwarders) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to view an affected container could query the Representational State Transfer (REST) API for approvals to retrieve a live external prompt link belonging to another user. Using this link, the user could read the approval prompt without authentication and submit a response, potentially disrupting or altering the automated workflow governed by that approval.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API for approvals exposes the live external prompt link without verifying that the requester owns the approval.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an unauthenticated user could gain administrator privileges through a user account that receives an unintended role. A user that holds a role with permission to create or modify users and assign roles must assign the target account a role with a numeric name through the user-management Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the API resolves a numeric role name as a role identifier instead of preserving the requested role name.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could cause Splunk SOAR to send a stored Elasticsearch password to a host that the user controls.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR reuses a stored Elasticsearch password for a changed Search Settings endpoint without requiring a replacement password.

In Splunk App for Stream versions below 8.1.7, an unauthenticated user who can reach the Splunk App for Stream Representational State Transfer (REST) API on the management port (8089) could upload an Extensible Markup Language (XML) vocabulary file, which lets the vocabulary upload endpoint read local files accessible to the Splunk process or send outbound requests.
The vulnerability is possible because the vocabulary upload endpoint parses uploaded XML without an application-level policy that blocks external entity resolution.
For more information see About Splunk Stream (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/collect-stream-data/install-and-configure-splunk-stream/8.1/introduction/about-splunk-stream) and restmap.conf (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/admin-manual/9.4/configuration-file-reference/9.4.3-configuration-file-reference/restmap.conf) in the Splunk documentation.

A vulnerability was determined in smartalock wireguard-lwip up to cfba91666590e86bd67842c71cedf9a423be823a. Impacted is the function mul of the file src/crypto/refc/x25519.c of the component X25519 Ladder. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to local privilege escalation via the SUID-root podman_wrapper binary on the Collector appliance. A local attacker with low-privileged access to the Collector can exploit insufficient argument validation in the SUID binary to execute arbitrary commands as root, resulting in full compromise of the Collector appliance.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java treats a complete field line that ends exactly at a known field-section boundary as incomplete and returns without consuming bytes. BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection then leaves fieldSectionLength unchanged and repeats the loop because its forward-progress checks are Java assertions, which are normally disabled in production. A remote peer that sends a known-length Binary HTTP header or trailer section ending at that boundary can make the parser spin indefinitely and pin the Netty event-loop or worker thread responsible for the channel. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

netty-incubator-codec-ohttp implements Oblivious HTTP (OHTTP) gateway and client functionality using Netty. Prior to 0.0.23.Final, BinaryHttpParser.readFieldSection in codec-bhttp/src/main/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/bhttp/BinaryHttpParser.java loops while fieldSectionLength is nonzero and relies on disabled-by-default assertions to require BinaryHttpParser.readFieldLine to return a value and consume bytes. A corrupt field line can consume more bytes than its understated declared section length and drive the counter negative, or a truncated field line can return without consuming data and leave the parser in the same state. An unauthenticated OHTTP peer can encrypt such Binary HTTP content under the gateway public configuration, reach OHttpRequestResponseContext.ContentDecoder.decodeChunk, and permanently pin a Netty event-loop thread at full CPU before application business logic. Multiple requests can exhaust the event-loop group and deny service until restart. This issue is fixed in version 0.0.23.Final.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via quadratic bigint loop in os2ip.

Every INTEGER or ENUMERATED longer than four content octets reaches os2ip, which iterates over each content octet with $result = ($result * 256) + $octet. Each multiplication operates on a bigint that grows by one octet per step, so decoding an n-octet value takes O(n^2) bigint work. Nothing limits content length before this loop runs.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a single oversized INTEGER or ENUMERATED value.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded MSG_PEEK buffer doubling in asn_recv.

asn_recv peeks the socket in a loop, doubling the buffer size on each pass until a tag and length can be decoded. An inverted boolean guard ($tb || rather than $tb &&) prevents the need-more-data exit from firing once a tag byte has been decoded. When asn_decode_length returns no value because the length is absent or incomplete, no exit fires for that case either. MSG_PEEK leaves socket data unconsumed, so each re-peek returns at once while the buffer size doubles.

A single truncated BER header sent to a process calling asn_recv doubles the peek buffer until memory is exhausted. Perl's realloc failure is fatal and not catchable with eval.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unchecked exponent length in binary REAL decoding.

Binary REAL decoding never bounds-checks the exponent length against the available content. For a minimal one-byte binary REAL, the exponent byte is read from outside the element, making the mantissa length -1. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the mantissa is nearly all of the input that follows the element. The long-form exponent path also omits the extra length octet when sizing the mantissa.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust CPU with a list of such values, as each mantissa loop iterates over the remaining input. The decoded values are also computed from bytes outside each element.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via exponent-notation string in INTEGER encoding.

The encoder routes any value with abs >= 2**31 to i2osp without validating that it is an integer. A string in exponent notation such as "1e8000" passes that threshold. Math::BigInt expands it to an 8001-digit integer, and i2osp's per-octet conversion loop is quadratic in that size.

An attacker who controls encoded INTEGER values can exhaust CPU with a short exponent-notation string.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via zero-length BIT STRING content.

A BIT STRING with zero content octets passes -1 to substr as the length. Perl reads a negative length as an offset from the end of the string, so the decoded value is nearly all of the input that follows the element. In the constructed form each zero-length segment copies the rest of the input again, so memory grows with the square of the input size.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a short constructed BIT STRING. The resulting value also contains bytes from adjacent input.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unlimited recursion depth in constructed-form string decoding.

Any constructed-form string element causes the decoder to recurse on the element's contents. The BER encoding controls nesting depth at four bytes per level, with no bound checked. Perl recursion is heap-allocated, so the process grows without a stack crash.

An attacker who controls the decoded data can exhaust memory with a small deeply nested constructed string.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via a declared element length passed unchecked to sysread in asn_read and asn_get.

The length an element declares in its BER header is passed to sysread as the read size. Perl grows the target buffer to that size before reading, so memory is allocated from the declared length, not from the data received. A 6-byte header can declare a length of up to 4GB.

A single header makes the reading process allocate the declared size. Where the allocation fails, perl exits with "Out of memory", which eval cannot catch.

Convert::ASN1 versions before 0.37 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via unbounded arc length in OBJECT IDENTIFIER decoding and encoding.

The content of an OBJECT IDENTIFIER or RELATIVE-OID element is passed to unpack "w*" on decode, and the arcs of an OID string to pack "w*" on encode. Perl converts each arc to or from its decimal string in time quadratic in the arc's length, and nothing limits that length.

An attacker who controls the decoded data, or an OID string passed to encode, can exhaust CPU with a single oversized arc.
PowerLink developed by Neotroni Lighting has a SQL Injection vulnerability, allowing unauthenticated remote attackers to inject arbitrary SQL commands to read database contents.

A flaw was found in crun. When copying files onto a tmpfs mounted with tmpcopyup, crun opens the destination a second time by name. A container that shares a writable volume with the container being created can change that path between the two lookups, so crun copies image files onto host files, including files under /proc/sys.

The Lightbox with PhotoSwipe WordPress plugin before 5.19.0 does not escape image link URLs before outputting them in the attributes of the lightbox share menu, allowing unauthenticated users to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks via comments when the PhotoSwipe 4 frontend is used.

A flaw was found in the Kuadrant WebAssembly (WASM) shim shipped in Red Hat Connectivity Link 1.5. When a TokenRateLimitPolicy is attached to an HTTPRoute that also has an AuthPolicy - or when a RateLimitPolicy with defaults or overrides is attached to the Gateway or listener of such routes - the shim's action pipeline fails to dispatch the authentication guard at request time, and the request is forwarded upstream. Unauthenticated requests return 200 OK instead of 401, and neither authentication nor rate limiting is enforced. Both policies continue to report Enforced, leaving no status-level indication of the failure.

The King Addons for Elementor – 100+ Elementor Widgets, 4 000+ Elementor Templates, WooCommerce Builder, Mega Menu, Popup Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 51.1.89. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary post meta values — including private contact data, API keys, license keys, and plugin-internal metadata — for any published post by supplying an arbitrary meta key name via the unauthenticated AJAX endpoint. The nonce check present in the handler provides no effective barrier because the nonce is emitted into every front-end page for logged-out visitors via wp_localize_script.

The rtMedia for WordPress, BuddyPress and bbPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'custom_fields' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.7.17 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The upload endpoint's only access control is a nonce check, and the 'rtmedia_upload_nonce' value is localized to every unauthenticated visitor on every front-end page via wp_enqueue_scripts, making it freely obtainable without an account.
Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference vulnerability in ReviewX ReviewX reviewx allows XML Entity Linking.This issue affects ReviewX: from n/a through 3.0.1.
Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in weDevs WP ERP erp allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects WP ERP: from n/a through 1.17.11.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Backup For WP WP Database Backup wp-database-backup allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Database Backup: from n/a through 7.14.

The VidShop for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in versions up to, and including, 1.10.0 via the /vsfw/v1/products/{id} REST API endpoint. This is due to the endpoint's permission_callback (check_public_permission) returning true unconditionally and the get_item() handler only checking that the product and video exist — it does not check the product's post_status or catalog visibility, nor does it verify that the product is actually linked to the supplied video_id. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to enumerate product IDs and read private, draft, and catalog-hidden WooCommerce products' names, short descriptions, prices, variations, attributes, and stock information that would otherwise be hidden from public view.

In the nrfconnect/ncs-zigbee repository, the GitHub Actions workflow
.github/workflows/build_documentation.yml used the pull_request_target trigger
while checking out and executing untrusted pull request code. This allowed a
pull request from a fork to run attacker-controlled code in the base repository
context with a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents: write, pages: write,
pull-requests: write), enabling remote code execution in CI, token
exfiltration, and unauthorized modification of repository content and GitHub
Pages. The workflow was disabled and then rewritten to remove the issue.

The Mang Board plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion via Path Traversal in versions up to, and including, 2.4.8 via the `file_path` column handled by the `mbw_board_files_api_body()` function. The plugin stores an attacker-supplied value directly into the files admin table (no realpath, dot-segment, or directory-containment filtering) and later concatenates it onto `MBW_UPLOAD_PATH` before passing the result to `@unlink()`. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server, including `wp-config.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in RomanCode MapSVG mapsvg-lite-interactive-vector-maps allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects MapSVG: from n/a through 9.0.5.

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, a BASIC application user, or an unauthenticated visitor to a public write form, can store markup in a shared external datasource that a builder or administrator later evaluates in any Handlebars binding Preview that surfaces the value, including the Data-section Formula column editor or any binding drawer. jsonFormatter.format() in packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts leaves raw strings and object keys unescaped, while packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte inserts the formatted result as raw HTML. The Handlebars SafeString path preserves the attacker-controlled value, and the Builder origin lacks a Content-Security-Policy that would block the resulting script. This permits stored script execution in the higher-privileged builder or administrator session rather than the writer's own role, allowing privileged Builder API actions and workspace data access. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

svglib reads SVG files and converts them to other formats. Prior to 2.3.1, the svg2rlg() renderer recursively expands nested SVG <use> references by deep-copying each referenced subtree; SvgRenderer.renderUse() in src/svglib/svglib.py calls xlink_href_target(), which rejects direct cycles but permits acyclic reference graphs with repeated fan-out. A small attacker-controlled SVG can therefore trigger exponentially increasing node expansion, consuming excessive CPU and memory in any application that renders it without a non-default option; HTML-to-PDF workflows using xhtml2pdf can reach the same renderer when an embedded data:image/svg+xml image in an HTML img element is passed to pisa.CreatePDF(). This issue is fixed in 2.3.1.

A flaw was found in KubeVirt/containerized-data-importer. When a VirtualMachine with an embedded DataVolumeTemplate carrying the cdi.kubevirt.io/storage.checkStaticVolume annotation and a cross-namespace clone source is created by a tenant, the service-account clone authorization check can be bypassed, allowing a PVC from another namespace to be cloned into the tenant's namespace without the required permissions. This can result in cross-tenant data disclosure.

SportEase is a web application for managing school sports events, class rosters, and competition teams. Prior to 1.3, an authenticated account with is_profile_complete=false can submit an attacker-selected class_id for any class in the currently active event to PUT /api/user/profile during first profile completion. AuthHandler.UpdateProfile accepts the class without validating the user's legitimate membership and automatically derives and assigns the corresponding {class_name}_rep role while isFirstCompletion is true. The attacker can become representative of one selected class, view roster information including email addresses, and add or remove competition-team assignments. Downstream handlers correctly reject access to other classes, so the impact is bounded to the selected class, but the representative privilege cannot be revoked through the exposed API and requires direct database intervention or another out-of-band remediation method. This issue is fixed in version 1.3.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, libatalk/dsi/dsi_stream.c interprets the dsi_code and dsi_doff union field as a data offset for all DSI command types instead of limiting that interpretation to DSIWrite. An unauthenticated client can send a non-WRITE DSIFUNC_CMD packet with a nonzero dsi_code smaller than dsi_len, causing dsi_stream_receive to consume only the dsi_code number of payload bytes and leave attacker-controlled bytes in the readahead buffer. The residual bytes become the next DSI header, allowing protocol desynchronization that can close sessions, corrupt protocol state, or trigger an infinite-read denial of service. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

The SMSC911x/LAN9220 Ethernet driver stages every outgoing frame in a fixed-size static buffer before pushing it to the controller FIFO. eth_tx() in drivers/ethernet/eth_smsc911x.c took the frame length from net_pkt_get_len(pkt) and passed it directly to net_pkt_read(pkt, tx_buf, total_len), with no comparison against the size of tx_buf (NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE). net_pkt_read() takes no destination size and only fails when the packet is shorter than the requested length, so any packet longer than the staging buffer was copied past its end.

Nothing between the IP layer and the driver bounds the frame to what the link can carry: ethernet_send() in subsys/net/l2/ethernet/ethernet.c performs no length check, and the IPv6 output path only compares the packet against the interface MTU when CONFIG_NET_IPV6_FRAGMENT is enabled (it is disabled by default). The size the stack will build is therefore governed by the interface MTU, and that MTU is remotely settable: handle_ra_input() in subsys/net/ip/ipv6_nbr.c honours the MTU option of any Router Advertisement with a value up to 0xffff, gated only by the standard hop-limit-255 and link-local-source checks. An unauthenticated attacker on the same link can raise the MTU and then have the device emit a single frame of several kilobytes, for example as a TCP segment from any service that returns more than ~1.5 KB or as an oversized UDP datagram.

The result is an out-of-bounds write into .bss immediately after tx_buf, with the overrun length and much of its content derived from the transmitted frame. Consequences range from corruption of adjacent kernel data and a crash to potential control-flow influence where the clobbered globals hold pointers; the practical overrun size is bounded by the network buffer pool rather than by the advertised MTU. The fix rejects frames larger than NET_ETH_MAX_FRAME_SIZE with -EMSGSIZE before any TX_DATA_PORT write, so the controller FIFO is also not left holding a command word without its payload.

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in Datasolution AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter acymailing allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects AcyMailing SMTP Newsletter: from n/a through 11.1.0.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.00, a network attacker who can alter outbound traffic to the extension store can exploit the HTTP client's disabled sslverify setting to substitute a serialized response. Extension-store handlers pass the response to unserialize() without an allowed_classes restriction, allowing an in-tree GuzzleHttp\Cookie\FileCookieJar gadget to write attacker-controlled content to a chosen path. When a GODADMIN opens or uses the store list, detail, install, or update functions, the substituted response can write a PHP file under the web root and execute code as the web-server user. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.00.

MapServer is a system for developing web-based GIS applications. From 4.4.0 until 8.6.5, an unauthenticated remote attacker can send a WCS GetCoverage XML POST request whose BoundingBox element omits the crs attribute, causing xmlGetProp() in src/mapwcs.cpp to return null. msWCSParseRequest() then calls string functions on the null value before normal WCS exception handling, crashing the CGI or FastCGI worker. The analogous KVP or GET path is not affected because it obtains a count-validated, non-null token. A single request can terminate one worker, and repeated requests can exhaust a fixed worker pool and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 8.6.5.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.12 and 4.6.02, an attacker who can reach an image-upload flow can upload a valid image with appended PHP short-tag code and a double-extension filename. NukeViet\Files\Upload::save_file() relied on verify_image(), which missed the <? short-open tag, while filename handling preserved embedded dots, validation inspected only the final extension, and an .htaccess rule blocked PHP extensions only at the end of the URI. On Apache mod_php systems configured with short_open_tag and a PHP extension handler, the stored polyglot can execute as PHP and run operating-system commands as the web-server user; PHP-FPM, nginx, and end-anchored handler configurations are not exposed to the execution step. This issue is fixed in versions 4.5.12 and 4.6.02.

U.S Department of the Interior Unstable Slope Management Program contains a vulnerable endpoint that allows an unauthenticated attacker, without a cookie header, to send a POST request resulting in the creation of a new user. Fixed on or around 2026-10-19.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/agents/actions/:agent_id in api/server/routes/agents/actions.js loads an existing action with owner credentials and merges editor-controlled metadata.domain and metadata.raw_spec while preserving metadata.api_key and related OAuth client secrets. A collaborator with EDIT permission can repoint an action to an attacker-controlled host, and a later tool invocation decrypts and sends the retained owner credential to that destination. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

probe-image-size before 7.5.0 contains an algorithmic-complexity denial of service vulnerability in lib/exif_utils.js that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying self-referencing EXIF IFDs. Attackers can submit a crafted 9.6 KB JPEG with repeated ExifIFD and InteropIFD pointers to block the Node.js event loop for about 23 seconds.

devpi-web before 5.2.0 contains an unauthenticated path traversal vulnerability in the +doc documentation route because docs_file_exists and docs_file_path in doczip.py never confine relpath to the documentation directory. Attackers can request a relpath with a leading // or percent-encoded .. segments to read server files, including the keyfs sqlite database holding password hashes.

Qwik City before 1.20.3 (@builder.io/qwik-city) and @qwik.dev/router before 2.0.0-rc.4 contain an improperly controlled object modification vulnerability in formToObj that allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite built-in function properties. Attackers can send a form POST with nested field names traversing inherited members of string values, breaking Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call process-wide until server restart.

SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.8.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated Readers to read protected documents through block-reference footnote resolution in Markdown export. Attackers can request copyStdMarkdown for a public document referencing a hidden, disabled, or password-protected document to disclose its body text without the publish password.

OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.

Frappe Framework before 15.120.1 and 16.x before 16.33.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in file attachment handling that permits arbitrary file read. Authenticated attackers holding a single ordinary role without write permissions can abuse attachment handling to read server files outside the application boundary.

Frappe ERPNext 4.3.0 before 15.121.6 and 16.x before 16.37.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in an endpoint of the Selling and Buying modules, where a request value validated early can be overridden by caller-supplied data that reaches a database query unvalidated. Any authenticated user, including a portal user with no roles, can send crafted requests to extract sensitive data, including active session data, and take over other accounts such as administrators.

Frappe ERPNext 10.1.41 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Manufacturing module endpoint that replaces BOMs without checking whether the caller may modify either BOM or the affected assemblies. Authenticated users who can create a BOM Update Log can send a crafted request naming two BOMs to replace the first with the second in every assembly site-wide.

Frappe ERPNext 8.11.1 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 is missing an authorization check in print and portal views, which fail to apply desk users' User Permissions to customer documents. Authenticated desk users with an ordinary job role can send crafted requests naming records outside their permitted scope to read documents of customers their User Permissions exclude.

Frappe ERPNext 6.3.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the customer and supplier portal list endpoint, which returns complete selling documents and RFQs without checking permission on the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can request out-of-scope records to read valuation, margin, and other bidder details.

Frappe ERPNext 11.1.7 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Regional module endpoint that returns private e-invoice files after checking only document-type permissions, not per-record User Permissions. Authenticated attackers with a common operational role can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to read other companies' private e-invoice files.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns uploaded bank statement file content without checking record-level permissions. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming records outside their scope to read full statement file contents.

Frappe ERPNext 4.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns the taxes and charges of documents without checking record permissions. Authenticated users, including portal users or users with no roles, can request arbitrary document types and records to read tax rows beyond their permitted scope.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns Item master records without checking whether the caller may read the requested records. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests naming out-of-scope records to retrieve complete item data including costing and purchase rates.

Frappe ERPNext 16.0.0 before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Manufacturing module endpoint that allows authenticated users to cancel Stock Reservation Entries without record-level write permission. Low-privilege attackers can send crafted requests naming manufacturing documents of other companies or outside their User Permissions to release reserved stock and disrupt stock allocation.

Frappe ERPNext before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that records bank clearance dates, which checks only a broad role permission before writing to caller-named payment documents. Authenticated Accounts Users can send crafted requests naming payment documents of other companies, outside their User Permissions, or already submitted, to alter clearance dates and compromise bank reconciliation integrity.

Frappe ERPNext 15.8.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an endpoint shared across modules that returns transaction child table rows without checking permissions on the child table or parent document. Authenticated attackers, including portal users or users without roles, can supply document types and filter conditions to read business document line details and probe record values.

Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in Erlang OTP public_key (pubkey_ocsp module) allows OCSP designated-responder authorization bypass via missing signature verification.

The OCSP response validation in public_key:pkix_ocsp_validate/5 does not verify that a CA-designated responder certificate was cryptographically signed by the issuing CA. Instead, it only checks that the responder certificate's issuer name matches the CA's subject name and that the certificate has the OCSPSigning extended key usage. An attacker who can intercept or control OCSP responses can create a self-signed certificate with a matching issuer name and the OCSPSigning EKU, and use it to forge OCSP responses that mark revoked certificates as valid.

This affects SSL/TLS clients using OCSP stapling, which may accept connections to servers with revoked certificates, potentially transmitting sensitive data to compromised servers. Applications using the public_key:pkix_ocsp_validate/5 API directly are also affected, with impact depending on usage context.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/public_key/src/pubkey_ocsp.erl and program routines pubkey_ocsp:is_authorized_responder/3.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 27.0 before OTP 27.3.4.10 and OTP 28.4.2, corresponding to public_key from 1.16 before 1.17.1.2 and 1.20.3, and ssl from 11.2 before 11.2.12.7 and 11.5.4.

A flaw was found in gnutls. Servers configured with RSA-PSK (Rivest–Shamir–Adleman – Pre-Shared Key) wrongfully matched usernames containing a NUL character with truncated usernames. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending a specially crafted username, leading to an authentication bypass. This vulnerability allows an attacker to gain unauthorized access by circumventing the authentication process.

Origin Validation Error vulnerability in ninenines gun (gun_http2 module) allows cross-origin cookie injection via unvalidated HTTP/2 PUSH_PROMISE authority.

In gun_http2:push_promise_frame/7, the :authority pseudo-header from an incoming PUSH_PROMISE frame is stored verbatim into the promised stream record without checking that it matches the connection's origin. When gun_http2:headers_frame/9 later processes the response headers for the promised stream, it calls gun_cookies:set_cookie_header/7 with the unvalidated server-supplied authority before any status branching and before user code can act. This violates RFC 7540 §10.6 / RFC 9113 §8.4, which require receivers to treat as a protocol error any push for a resource the server is not authoritative for.

A malicious or compromised HTTP/2 server can plant cookies scoped to arbitrary third-party domains into the client's shared cookie store. This enables session fixation attacks against those domains and, if the planted cookie overrides a legitimate session token, may result in account takeover. No user interaction beyond making a normal HTTP/2 request to the attacker-controlled server is required.

This issue affects gun: from 2.0.0-pre.2 before 2.4.0.

The Erlang/OTP ssl TLS 1.2 (and earlier) and DTLS client does not verify that the cipher suite selected by the server in ServerHello was among the suites offered by the client in ClientHello. The client-side tls_handshake:hello/5 handler validates the negotiated protocol version and the downgrade sentinel but hands the server-chosen suite directly to ssl_handshake:handle_server_hello_extensions/9, which installs it without a membership check. The TLS 1.3 client path performs this check (per RFC 8446), so it is not affected.

An on-path attacker between the client and the intended server can respond with a ServerHello selecting an anonymous key exchange suite such as TLS_DH_anon_* or TLS_ECDH_anon_* that the client never offered. Anonymous suites do not require the server to present a certificate, so the entire verify_peer and cacerts configuration is bypassed: the attacker completes the handshake with its own ephemeral parameters, no certificate is validated, no hostname is checked, and ssl:connect returns {ok, Socket}. All subsequent application traffic is readable and modifiable by the attacker.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 27.3.4.15, OTP 28.5.0.4, and OTP 29.0.4, corresponding to ssl from 5.3.4 before 11.2.12.11, 11.6.0.4, and 11.7.4. Whether OTP before OTP 17.0, corresponding to ssl before 5.3.4, is affected is unknown.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in ash-project ash allows an unauthenticated attacker to inject a filter expression through a forged keyset pagination cursor, resulting in SQL injection or code execution depending on the data layer.

Read actions with keyset pagination decode the client-supplied page[:after] or page[:before] cursor in decode_values/2 in lib/ash/page/keyset.ex using non_executable_binary_to_term/2 with [:safe]. That guard blocks new atoms, funs, and ports, but not a struct built from atoms already interned in a running Ash application, so a decoded %Ash.Query.Call{} expression survives and is spliced into the keyset filter as a comparison value in do_filters/4 and evaluated. Because the cursor bypasses the Ash.Expr macro, the runtime never applies the private?/public? gate that would otherwise reject it. On AshPostgres the injected fragment is inlined into the SQL query; on the ETS and Simple data layers it is evaluated in-process as an arbitrary function call.

This issue affects ash: from 1.17.0 before 3.31.3.

knowns through 0.36.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the POST /api/embedding-models/test endpoint that issues outbound requests to caller-supplied destinations without validation. Attackers can enumerate internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints by observing transport error messages that reveal network reachability information.
Stack-based buffer overflow in SysInternals allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

A vulnerability has been found in FlowCI flow-core-x up to 1.23.49. The affected element is the function ConditionManagerImpl.run of the file core/src/main/java/com/flowci/core/common/manager/ConditionManagerImpl.java of the component Groovy Script Evaluation. The manipulation of the argument condition leads to code injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.11 and 4.2.0 pre-releases before 4.2.0-beta.3 contain an account enumeration vulnerability in the unauthenticated POST /api/webauthn/prepare-login endpoint, which returns stable stored credential IDs for passkey-registered accounts but an md5(time())-derived fallback ID otherwise. Unauthenticated attackers can compare allowCredentials IDs from requests sent more than one second apart, without rate limiting, to identify existing passkey-registered accounts and their credential IDs.

OpenEMR before 8.4.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the server send HTTP requests by registering an OAuth2 client with an unvalidated jwks_uri. Attackers can trigger the fetch via the token introspection endpoint with an unsigned client_assertion to probe internal services and reach cloud metadata endpoints.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains an integer underflow in ccmp_decrypt() in src/ec_encryption_ccmp.c that subtracts the 8-byte CCMP trailer without checking minimum length. Attackers on a network whose WPA key is loaded can send a short crafted CCMP frame to overflow a stack buffer in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

OpenMage magento-lts before 20.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the TinyMCE WYSIWYG editor fails to filter scripts in specially crafted HTML tags. Attackers can inject an img element with a malicious onmouseover attribute to execute scripts in the browsers of users viewing the rendered content.

A post-authentication command injection vulnerability in the “Description” parameter of a CGI program  in Zyxel DX3300-T0 firmware versions through 5.50(ABVY.8.3)C0 could allow an authenticated attacker with administrator privileges to execute OS commands by sending a crafted HTTP request.

WP File Manager before 8.0.7 contains a file upload restriction bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to upload arbitrary PHP files by exploiting a misconfigured elFinder connector in file_folder_manager.php where an empty uploadDeny list causes allowPutMime() to unconditionally return true, bypassing the uploadAllow restriction. Attackers can upload a .php file directly or upload it under an allowed filename and then rename it via the rename connector command, achieving remote code execution as the web server user.

Nexterm through 1.2.2-BETA contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows users with permissions.manage to gain unauthorized permissions because addGroupMember and setUserGroups lack the grantsBeyondCaller check. Attackers can add their own account to custom groups via the group membership endpoints to inherit permissions like users.impersonate and settings.backup.

Improper state validation in Network in Google Chrome prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker to potentially bypass web origin policy via crafted network traffic. (Chromium security severity: Low)
Confused deputy in Grid in Google Chrome on on Android prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a remote attacker to bypass web origin policy via crafted network traffic. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Pi-hole FTL is the core engine of the Pi-hole network-level advertisement and tracker blocker. From 6.6.2 until 6.7, PATCH /api/config accepts unfiltered CivetWeb lua_* options through webserver.advancedOpts, while POST /api/teleporter writes attacker-controlled content from a dhcp.leases archive entry through src/zip/teleporter.c without content validation. An authenticated administrator can place controlled file content on disk, point a Lua execution option at that file, and rely on the advancedOpts configuration change to restart FTL. CivetWeb then executes the file as Lua through the processing in src/webserver/webserver.c, allowing arbitrary commands to run as the pihole operating-system user and persist across restarts while the configuration and file remain. This issue is fixed in version 6.7.

The Slimbox plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment (anchor title within comment HTML)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. WordPress core comment KSES permits unauthenticated commenters to post anchor elements with href and title attributes, so an entity-encoded payload stored in the title attribute survives sanitization verbatim; the browser then decodes the entities when populating the DOM .title property, and the Slimbox library's jQuery .html() caption sink renders it as executable HTML.

Successful exploitation requires a logged-in user, typically an administrator, to click the attacker's image link in the comment; however, because unmoderated comments appear in the WordPress moderation queue where administrators routinely interact with them, the moderation gate does not meaningfully prevent exploitation. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions up to and including 9.3.6, middie does not honor the router's caseSensitive setting and matches path-scoped middleware mount paths with a case-insensitive regular expression that does not fold non-ASCII characters, while Fastify's router, when caseSensitive is set to false, lowercases the request path with a Unicode-aware conversion that maps the KELVIN SIGN character (U+212A) to the ASCII letter k. A request that spells a k in a protected mount path as the percent-encoded KELVIN SIGN is therefore routed to the protected handler while the middleware mounted on that path, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, never matches and is skipped, letting an unauthenticated client reach the handler. Only applications that set caseSensitive to false and protect a mount path containing the letter k are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, or keep routing case-sensitive, which is the default.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine that adds Express and Connect style middleware support to Fastify. In versions 8.3.0 through 9.3.6, the internal helper that normalizes a path-scoped middleware's mount path only handles string inputs, but the use method also accepts an array of mount paths and passes it through unchanged, so the normalization silently does nothing. As a result, a trailing slash on an array element survives into the generated route-matching regular expression, and an element that is exactly the root path, meaning a catch-all mount, is dropped entirely. Requests to subroutes of the affected mount paths then skip the path-scoped middleware, such as authentication, authorization, or rate limiting, while Fastify's router still dispatches them to the handler, allowing an unauthenticated client to reach protected routes. Applications are affected when they mount middleware on an array of paths in which an element ends with a slash, including one introduced by a plugin prefix that ends with a slash, or is exactly the root path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.7, and users should upgrade to 9.3.7 or later. As a workaround, enforce authorization in a Fastify hook such as preHandler that runs after routing, and avoid array mount paths with a trailing slash element for security relevant middleware.

Attackers with the CA certificate and one observed leaf certificate can regenerate that host's leaf private key and impersonate the host to clients trusting the proxy CA.

United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A Download of Code Without Integrity Check Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows network-adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of United Chargers Grizzl-E Smart 40A EV chargers. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of OCPP messages. The issue results from the lack of proper verification of firmware integrity prior to installation. An attacker can leverage this in conjunction with other vulnerabilities to execute code in the context of the device. Was ZDI-CAN-28957.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows administrators to include arbitrary server files by storing ../ sequences in the content manager file name. Unauthenticated requests to shop_content.php then pass the stored path to include(), executing embedded PHP in uploaded content files or images as the web server user.
