NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Prover9Parent.config_prover9 and Mace accept a relative binary_location and pass it to find_binary as path_to_bin, disabling the bare-name absolute-path guard. A local attacker who can plant prover9 or mace4 in the resolved working directory can cause subprocess.Popen to execute that binary with the invoking user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Poweradmin is a web-based DNS administration tool for PowerDNS server. From 4.0.0 until 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1, lib/Domain/Service/MfaService.php verifies email second-factor codes through MfaService::verifyCode() without limiting failed attempts, and lib/Application/Controller/MfaVerifyController.php logs failures without throttling them. An attacker who knows the user's password can repeatedly guess the six-digit code during its ten-minute validity period when email MFA is enabled, potentially bypassing the second factor; the advisory notes MFA is disabled by default and that the practical request rate was not measured. This issue is fixed in versions 4.2.6, 4.3.5, and 4.4.1.

An improper neutralization of delimiters in the MongoDB C# driver's DNS SRV connection-string resolution lets an unauthenticated party who can answer the client's DNS SRV query place a host outside the trusted domain into the client's server list. When an application resolves the connection string through the affected API and connects with the result, application data, authentication credentials and query results may pass through that host. This may result in unintended disclosure of data and credentials and in forged query results.

In Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_user" Splunk Enterprise Security role could add attacker-controlled values to lookup data used by the Primary Functions report. If another authenticated user later selects the value in the Primary Function Summary panel, the Splunk App for Payment Card Industry Compliance could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selected the value. With this access, the first user could expose or modify data available to the user who selected the value.
The vulnerability is possible because the Primary Functions report does not safely escape report values before including them in drilldown searches.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Reports (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/user-manual/8.7/using-the-splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/reports) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the run_collect capability could store attacker-controlled values in Updates data. If another user who can access the System Update Status report selects an affected row, Splunk Enterprise Security could run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who selects the row. The user who stores the values could then access sensitive data and modify data available to the user who selects the row.
The vulnerability is possible because the System Update Status report does not validate destination, signature, and vendor-product values before inserting them into drilldown searches.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) and System Update Status (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/splunk-app-for-pci-compliance/installation-and-configuration-manual/8.7/configure-reports/system-update-status) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission and restricted tenant access could modify settings for a tenant outside the role scope through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. With this access, the user could expose confidential tenant environment values, alter tenant settings and automation behavior, or take the tenant out of operation.
The vulnerability is possible because the Tenant REST API checks the System Settings edit permission but does not enforce the tenant restrictions for the role before it updates the selected tenant.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises), Configure multiple tenants on your Splunk SOAR (On-premises) instance (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.7.0/configure-product-settings-for-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance/configure-multiple-tenants-on-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-instance), and REST Tenant (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/8.5.0/multi-tenancy-endpoints/rest-tenant) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could execute arbitrary code on the host that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API accepts package references from untrusted sources and passes them to the dependency installer.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use a customer automation dependency to execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not properly separate customer automation dependencies from trusted product code.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use the Automation Dependency Wheel Representational State Transfer (REST) API to write arbitrary files outside the intended directory, which could lead to arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict uploaded automation dependency wheel filenames to the intended storage directory.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with local access to the affected host could obtain a live Splunk SOAR session token or decrypted asset configuration when another user starts an App Editor debug action.
The vulnerability is possible because App Editor debug actions expose sensitive runtime information to other local users on the affected host.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with access to the configured load balancer account could replace a load balancer helper that Splunk SOAR later runs with root privileges during cluster lifecycle operations. If a Splunk SOAR administrator performs a cluster lifecycle operation, Splunk SOAR could execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the load balancer.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify the integrity or ownership of the load balancer helper before running it with root privileges.

The MongoDB Java driver applies its DNS seedlist domain restriction to a record value that is later re-interpreted differently when the connection target is parsed, so the name that is checked and the name that is used can differ. An unauthenticated party who can set or forge the DNS service record for the seed domain in a connection string can cause the driver to direct its session to an unrelated host and to complete certificate verification against that host instead. This may result in unintended disclosure of application data and of configured database credentials, and in unintended content being returned to the application as query results.

baserCMS is a website development framework. From 5.2.3 until 5.3.0, BcThemeFileService::getFullpath() in plugins/bc-theme-file/src/Service/BcThemeFileService.php skips its path containment check when realpath() fails for a nonexistent theme subdirectory selected by the type parameter. An authenticated administrator can supply a traversal path through the theme-file API to access locations outside the theme directory. The bypass of the CVE-2026-30940 fix can permit file writes, overwrites or deletion within the PHP process permissions and, where executable PHP can be written, remote code execution. This issue is fixed in 5.3.0.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in Apache Tomcat could occur during a request dispatch if the request depended on a security-role-ref provided by the dispatch target.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

The fix for CVE-2026-25854 was incomplete.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.19 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.53 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.116 through 9.0.123.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

A vulnerability has been found in sumiie24 School-Management-System up to d946d649c7c95e101fc5679ecd91999533bb10d7. The affected element is an unknown function of the file parent_Registration.php. Such manipulation of the argument student_reg leads to sql injection. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable.

A security vulnerability has been detected in rajesh2211 Doctor-Appointment-System up to ee974dcf4c50da85e6ea026e27f4370e9468b3cc. Affected is an unknown function of the file AppointmentSystem/AppointmentSystem/Connectivity.php of the component Login. The manipulation of the argument User leads to sql injection. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product is using a rolling release to provide continious delivery. Therefore, no version details for affected nor updated releases are available.

Multiple products produced by Ruijie Networks Co., Ltd. contain an OS command injection vulnerability that may lead to arbitrary OS commands being executed by an attacker with the administrative privilege.

The Charitable – Donation & Fundraising Platform (Donation Forms, Recurring Donations & Fundraising Campaigns) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'stripe_payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.15.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the nopriv AJAX endpoint is publicly obtainable from any rendered campaign donation form, making exploitation trivially accessible to unauthenticated visitors on sites with Stripe configured as a payment gateway.

The Apaczka.pl WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '_apaczka[<id>][error_messages] (and sibling subkeys inside _apaczka[])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable during WooCommerce classic guest checkout because WooCommerce's legacy order storage fires the save_post action with the checkout $_POST still populated, giving unauthenticated attackers a direct write path to order post meta without an authenticated session.

The PagBank / PagSeguro e Vindi para WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'customer.name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.1.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload can be planted via the legitimate hosted-checkout (Checkout PB) flow simply by entering it as a customer name on PagBank's payment page, requiring no hash brute-forcing whatsoever; the woocommerce_api_rm_ps_notif webhook path is additionally exploitable because its only gate is a 5-character (20-bit) truncated wp_hash() that is trivially brute-forceable.

The Kognetiks Chatbot plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.5.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The TeX payload survives WordPress core comment kses intact because it contains no HTML tags, and MathJax is active on fresh installs by default due to the 'chatbot_chatgpt_enable_mathjax' option defaulting to 'Yes' with no page or shortcode presence guard on enqueue.

The FV Flowplayer Video Player plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.5.57.7212 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's 'Parse Vimeo and YouTube links' setting to be enabled, which wires do_shortcode into the comment_text filter chain and allows the [fvplayer] shortcode to be rendered from comment content.

The Events Made Easy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event[event_notes]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable when the plugin's 'Allow guest submit?' Frontend Submit option is enabled, though the required nonce is freely obtainable by any anonymous visitor as it is printed on every frontend page.

A weakness has been identified in blinkospace blinko up to 1.8.8. Affected is an unknown function of the file /api/auth/verify-2fa of the component 2FA Endpoint. This manipulation of the argument userId causes improper authentication. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. Upgrading to version 1.8.9 is able to address this issue. Patch name: 80e1c4ffaffe66a97df2b5d85fad864ff3691dc8. Upgrading the affected component is advised.

The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'IPTC 2#120 (caption) / 2#005 (title) inside the image file' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an authenticated user with image-edit permissions to import an attacker-supplied image file, which is the plugin's standard workflow for photographer uploads, client galleries, and contest submissions.

The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the plugin's "What must the lightbox be applied to?" setting (thumbEffectContext) to be configured as "Try to apply to all images" or "Try to apply to all images that link to image files," which is not the shipping default, and also requires the attacker's comment to reach a publicly rendered state.

The NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 via the 'ajax_pagination_referrer' request parameter used on the /ngg_tag/<tag>/ taxonomy page. This is due to the plugin reading the pagination base URL from $_REQUEST, preserving the attacker-supplied host on the tag route (where ngg_wprouting_add_post_permalink is forced to false so the plugin does not re-base the links to the site's own permalink), and caching the fully rendered page in a transient keyed only on the request URI (not the request body) for 1800 seconds via NGG_RENDERING_CACHE / PHOTOCRATI_CACHE. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to poison the cached /ngg_tag/<tag>/ page so that its pagination links point to an attacker-controlled host; the plugin's own ajax_pagination.

The CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[].courier_code, data[].tracking_number (plus pp_sign for the auth bypass)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The authentication bypass is reachable only when the parcelpanel_api_key WordPress option is non-empty, which occurs automatically once an admin has opened or connected the ParcelPanel admin page; at that point any unauthenticated attacker can bypass the sole access gate by supplying a JSON boolean true as pp_sign, which PHP's loose == operator coerces to true when compared against the non-empty md5 hex string.

The Hydrogen Calendar Embeds plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via ICS Feed Event Fields (SUMMARY/DESCRIPTION/LOCATION) in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the attacker to have write access to an ICS feed that has been configured as a calendar source on the target WordPress site.

The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the AMP plugin to be active in Transitional or Standard template mode, and comments must be open on the target post, which is the WordPress default.

The Seraphinite Accelerator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.31 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has previously enabled the 'Enable logging' and 'HTTP trace' diagnostic options in the plugin's Advanced → Debug settings, both of which are disabled by default.

A vulnerability was detected in itsourcecode Banking Management System 1.0. This impacts an unknown function of the file manage_donation.php of the component Donor Management. The manipulation of the argument ID results in sql injection. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit is now public and may be used.

LessPass self-hosted sync server backend before commit 9469b0c lacks rate limiting on the JWT login endpoints /tokens/auth/ and /auth/jwt/create/, allowing unlimited authentication attempts. Unauthenticated remote attackers can brute force passwords or perform credential stuffing against known account emails to obtain tokens granting read and write access to stored profiles.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC string unmarshalling path in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses sl_unpack_cpx to calculate slen from qlen and the attacker-controlled used_in_last_block value without preventing a negative result. An authenticated AFP client can send a complex string or UTF-16 string element that makes slen negative, and the implicit conversion to size_t causes dalloc_strndup or convert_string_allocate to read beyond the heap buffer. The out-of-bounds read can expose heap data through the RPC response or crash the worker process. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. Prior to 4.4.3, the afpd Spotlight RPC unmarshalling loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c subtracts an attacker-controlled subcount from the unsigned count variable in sl_unpack_loop without verifying that subcount is not larger. An authenticated AFP client can place an excessive element count in the sl_unpack_ints, sl_unpack_uuid, sl_unpack_floats, or sl_unpack_date handler, or in a null element, so the subtraction wraps near UINT_MAX and the loop continues reading heap memory at increasing offsets up to toc_offset, which is capped at 65000. The out-of-bounds values can be stored in dalloc structures and returned in the Spotlight RPC response, disclosing heap contents. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.3.

pmo-platform is a modular PMO and release-management platform for Claude Code. Prior to 3.69.1, core/hooks/block-credential-reads.sh, core/hooks/block-egress.sh, core/hooks/block-fs-boundary.sh, and core/hooks/block-mcp-writes.sh pin PATH to /usr/bin:/bin, hard-code jq as /usr/bin/jq, and return success when jq is unavailable there. On systems where jq exists only in a Homebrew path, including affected pre-Sequoia or Homebrew-only macOS installations, the hooks can skip credential-read, network-egress, filesystem-boundary, and MCP-write controls. Native deny rules independently protect some credential paths but do not backstop the egress or MCP controls. An attacker who can influence a prompt, repository, or evaluation flow can use the skipped checks to expose secrets or perform unauthorized tool actions. This issue is fixed in version 3.69.1.
Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Brainstorm Force OttoKit suretriggers allows Server Side Request Forgery.This issue affects OttoKit: from n/a through 1.1.42.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.5.09, an unauthenticated attacker can submit the __serverInfoUpdate=1 field while controlling X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto. NukeViet\Core\Server::standardizeHost() did not validate the forwarded host against my_domains, and a trailing slash could preserve an attacker-selected port that server_info_update() used to construct a cURL request in includes/ini.php before authentication. The blind, HEAD-only request uses a fixed path, but it permits internal host and port discovery and can poison cached server_headers. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.09.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. In 4.6.00, an unauthenticated attacker can place the configured domain in X-Forwarded-Host while choosing a different destination in the ordinary Host header. The earlier fix validates only the forwarded value in includes/mainfile.php, while set_ini_file() in includes/ini.php constructs an outbound cURL request from the separately retained NV_SERVER_NAME before the ordinary host is rejected. Redirect following can carry the blind request to an attacker-selected private host, port, and path and invoke internal HTTP endpoints. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. Prior to 4.6.01, a super-administrator satisfying the NV_IS_SPADMIN gate can use modules/users/admin/fields.php to store an arbitrary existing PHP function in the func_callback setting for a custom profile field because the callback name is checked only with function_exists() and no allowlist restricts which function may be selected. modules/users/fields.check.php later invokes that function through call_user_func() when the field is validated through registration, profile editing, or administrator editing. Selecting a command-execution function crosses the super-administrator to operating-system boundary and executes commands as the web-server account, while ordinary users can trigger the stored callback after it is configured. Because the remediation validates callbacks only when they are written, upgrading does not remove a malicious callback already stored in the database, which must be cleaned manually. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

MaxKB is an open-source AI assistant for enterprise. Prior to 2.10.7-lts, custom Tool Init Param definitions accept attacker-controlled props_info.rules[].validator strings through POST /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool and PUT /admin/api/workspace/{workspace_id}/tool/{tool_id}, store them without restriction, and pass them to eval() when the parameter form renders. An authenticated user with the default USER workspace role can store JavaScript and trigger execution by opening the tool's Debug screen before entering or submitting a parameter value. The same Init Param form is exposed to accounts with edit permission on the tool, but execution by a different account was not independently verified. The confirmed script runs in the MaxKB origin; access to another user's bearer token and authenticated account authority is plausible only if that user renders the malicious form. This issue is fixed in version 2.10.7-lts.

G DATA Total Security Backup Service Uncontrolled Search Path Element Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of G DATA Total Security. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the Backup Service. The service restores archives from an unsecured location. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-28666.

A flaw has been found in hankcs HanLP up to 2.1.6. Impacted is the function uncompress of the file hanlp/utils/io_util.py of the component TAR Archive Extraction Handler. This manipulation causes path traversal. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version 2.1.7 is recommended to address this issue. Patch name: feb0f82d12762cf4e687b9926efd90c672857780. You should upgrade the affected component.

The Flutterwave Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'form_id' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The storing endpoint is accessible without authentication because the required nonce is publicly exposed on any front-end page rendering the plugin's [flw-pay-form], [flw-pay-button], or [flw-donation-form] shortcodes, allowing any unauthenticated visitor to scrape and reuse it.

The MetForm – Contact Form, Survey, Quiz, Conditional Forms, Form Templates & Custom Form Builder for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mf-te (the form-builder-chosen name of the Text Editor field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.3.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a published form containing a Text Editor block; the form's public markup exposes the submission nonce as data-form-nonce, allowing any unauthenticated visitor to satisfy the only submission barrier and store the malicious payload.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-N (rich-text draft value, saved as Save-and-Continue draft meta)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the targeted form to have a Rich-Text Textarea field with Save-and-Continue enabled and public submission permissions — once a crafted draft is saved, the payload executes whenever any user, including an administrator, resumes the draft or opens the Draft ID link from the Forminator Submissions screen.

The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'url' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that an administrator has added the Author URL column to the Comments screen layout and that the site accepts unauthenticated comments, both of which are default WordPress and plugin configurations.

The Admin Columns plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'HTTP_USER_AGENT' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The kses sanitization pass in classes/Sanitize/Kses.php uses wp_kses_allowed_html('post') augmented with iframe[src] and the data: protocol; because wp_kses_attr_check accepts any data-* attribute on any allowed tag without inspecting its value, a payload embedded inside a data-ac-tip attribute survives intact and is subsequently assigned to innerHTML by assets/js/table.js, bypassing the apparent mitigation entirely.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'upload-1 (the File Upload field's element_id)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This vulnerability is an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-1794; exploitation requires that the Forminator form's File Upload field is left at plugin defaults (no 'custom-files' restriction configured) and that the server maps no Content-Type to the .rtx extension — the default behavior of the Debian/Ubuntu Apache package used by the official WordPress Docker image and many shared hosts.

The EZ SQL Reports Shortcode Widget and DB Backup plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'User-Agent header (stored to comment_agent)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.26.45 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has saved a report whose SQL query selects attacker-controlled data such as comment_agent, and that the attacker can identify the saved report's slug — a condition trivially met when the administrator publishes the report on a public page via the [SQLREPORT] shortcode.

The Photo Gallery, Sliders, Proofing and Themes – NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.5.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the site administrator to have configured the Thickbox lightbox effect with the "Try to apply to all images" context (thumbEffectContext=all_images), and exploitation additionally depends on an administrator approving the attacker's initial comment so that subsequent comments from that author are auto-approved.

The Contact Form to Any API plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-message (any CF7 form field)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.0.7 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The malicious payload is stored via a single unauthenticated POST to Contact Form 7's public REST feedback endpoint, which uses permission_callback __return_true and requires no authentication or prior interaction to submit.

The WPBot – AI ChatBot for WordPress & Growth Suite: SEO, AI Writer, Email Marketing, Social Media plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'text' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 9.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit is triggered when an administrator opens the Chat Sessions screen, at which point the plugin's bundled Bootstrap 3.3.7 affix data-API passes the attacker-controlled data-target attribute value to jQuery as HTML, executing the injected script in the administrator's session.

The BlockStrap Page Builder – Bootstrap Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.1.65 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that the attacker has previously had at least one comment approved for a given name and email address, allowing subsequent comments from that author to bypass moderation under WordPress's default policy; exploitation is also limited to sites using a block theme, which is the WordPress default.

The SchemaEngine AI – AI Schema Markup, Reviews & Rich Snippets for SEO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via Comment Content via WebPage JSON-LD Description in all versions up to, and including, 3.1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the target page renders a core/latest-comments block with the displayExcerpt option enabled, causing comment content to be incorporated into the WebPage JSON-LD description output in wp_head.

The SiteOrigin CSS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'class' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires a Contributor-level or higher attacker to store a crafted class attribute value in a post, which then fires when a user with the edit_theme_options capability opens the Visual Inspector on the affected post and clicks anywhere in the preview iframe. Exploitation by unauthenticated attackers requires that a third-party plugin providing wp_kses_post()-filtered unauthenticated front-end submission is installed and configured, and a moderator approves the submission. On a default installation, where that is not configured, the vulnerability requires attackers with contributor-level access and above.

The Unbounce Landing Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.6. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the proxy error message that is persisted to the 'ub-proxy-error-message' option: unauthenticated attacker-controlled REQUEST_URI data is concatenated into the error string in UBHTTP::stream_request_curl()/stream_request_wp_remote() and stored via update_option(), then later echoed inside a <textarea> on the Unbounce Pages Diagnostics admin page without any escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user (an administrator viewing the Diagnostics screen) accesses an injected page.

The VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'inquiry (array keys)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The endpoint's only access gate is a CSRF token that is publicly emitted on the unauthenticated inquiry page, making the injection reachable by any unauthenticated visitor without any precondition beyond loading that public page.

The VikBooking Hotel Booking Engine & PMS plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'vbf<field_id>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.20 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The WP Fastest Cache – WordPress Cache Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary directory deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the singleDeleteCache function in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). Successful exploitation requires either the Custom Permalinks plugin or the GeoDirectory plugin to be co-installed, as these provide the necessary mechanism to write a traversal-bearing permalink value into the database that WP Fastest Cache then consumes without validation.

The WCFM Membership – WooCommerce Memberships for Multivendor Marketplace plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'wcfm_membership_registration_form[store_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.12.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the registration endpoint is publicly emitted on the /vendor-register/ page, making the endpoint fully reachable by unauthenticated attackers without any prior authentication or privilege escalation.

The Thim Kit for Elementor – Pre-built Templates & Widgets for Elementor plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires that the Post Comment widget is used with the Text Reveal entrance animation (Elementor class 'ekit--fx-word-reveal') on a Single Post template, and the comment widget must be within the initial viewport; once the first comment by an attacker is approved, or if comment moderation is disabled, subsequent payloads fire automatically for every visitor who loads the affected page.

The Germanized for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'billing_address.first_name (Store API checkout) → stored on parent order; withdrawal get_first_name() fallback' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.1.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload is planted via an unauthenticated guest checkout order's billing first name through the WooCommerce Store API, with execution triggered by a subsequent unauthenticated withdrawal request submission whose nonce is publicly available on the /withdraw-from-contract/ page.

The WPC Frequently Bought Together for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'variation' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 8.0.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce protecting the woobt_add_all_to_cart AJAX handler is emitted to all unauthenticated visitors via wp_localize_script, effectively nullifying the nonce as an authentication barrier and making the handler reachable without any login.

The One to one user Chat by WPGuppy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'userId' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.6 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The plugin's permission callback is trivially bypassed because it validates a JWT that the plugin itself signs using an attacker-supplied value from the guppy_guest_account cookie, and the guest code path (userType=0) skips the get_userdata() check that would confirm the userId corresponds to a real WordPress user.

The ElasticPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'orderby' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.3.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The injected payload is stored in the ep_query_log transient for up to 24 hours after a single unauthenticated frontend GET request, and only fires when an administrator subsequently opens the Status Report page and expands the Failed Queries panel.

The AutomatorWP – No-Code Workflow Automation, Integration & Webhooks Plugin, now with AI plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'your-message (any CF7 form field used in a form_field: tag)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 6.0.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have configured a public 'Guest submits a form' automation whose Send-an-email action embeds a form_field tag, after which the payload fires the next time any user opens the affected automation's email log entry.

The Paid Membership Plugin, Ecommerce, User Registration Form, Login Form, User Profile & Restrict Content – ProfilePress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'reg_bio' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.18.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The reg_bio parameter is accepted by the registration handler's allowlist even when the rendered registration form does not include a biography field, meaning an unauthenticated attacker can supply the payload via a raw POST request without needing a visible biography input on the form.

The wpForo Forum plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[display_name]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.2.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires public user registration to be enabled (users_can_register=1) and a valid _wpfnonce fetched from the public sign-up page, but is otherwise fully unauthenticated.

The Orphans plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.4.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a two-step comment chain: a benign first comment must be approved under a given name and email so that WordPress's comment_previously_approved mechanism auto-publishes the attacker's payload comment without moderation.

The Swift Performance Lite plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '<attacker-chosen parameter name>' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.3.7.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires that an administrator has configured at least one Cacheable AJAX Action via the plugin's AJAX Cache feature, a condition attackers can confirm by probing for a swift-performance: HIT response header.

The Accept Stripe Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'href of any <a> element containing 'asp_action=show_pp&product_id='' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that a user clicks the attacker-placed comment link to trigger the sink; however, if the non-default 'Prefetch Payment Popup Scripts' option is enabled, execution occurs on page load with no user interaction required.

A vulnerability was detected in eigent-ai eigent up to 1.0.2. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file backend/app/controller/chat_controller.py of the component Local Agent Control API. Performing a manipulation results in missing authentication. The attack may be initiated remotely. Upgrading to version 1.0.3 addresses this issue. The patch is named 59f43afcb1b0ba7b2de8c65d585124f196c4aa17. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the serveAssets route that allows unauthenticated attackers to read password-protected document assets via name collisions. Attackers can request GET /assets/<name> when a visible document references the same relative asset name, retrieving the protected file's contents on public-publish instances with Basic Auth disabled.

SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.6.2 and 3.7.3 before 3.8.10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/block/getDOMText endpoint, which renders caller-supplied DOM without checking publish access for referenced image paths. When publish authentication is disabled, anonymous visitors can submit DOM referencing a known unpublished, non-encrypted asset path to retrieve its already-cached OCR text.

SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to read indexed asset text referenced only by publish-disabled attribute-view rows. Attackers can request /api/asset/getDocAssets on a public host document to obtain the leaked asset path, then query /api/search/getAssetContentByPath to retrieve the confidential file's full indexed text.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain Administrator role by spoofing X-Forwarded-For through a loopback-trusted reverse proxy. Attackers can send requests with Host set to localhost and X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 to read private note-history contents via the /history/*path route when no lock-screen password is set.

Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows attackers to hijack SSO identities by planting local accounts with unverified victim emails. When emailfallback is enabled, attackers register or edit a local account using the victim's email, causing the victim's first OIDC login to link into the attacker-controlled account and expose their data.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its filesystem storage bucket that only canonicalizes the bucket root, not descendant symlinks. Attackers can reference paths through a pre-existing symlink inside the bucket that pass the lexical prefix check, reading and writing files across the host filesystem.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its bucket storage layer on Windows, where ObjectKey::check_no_traversal splits object keys only on forward slashes while FileStore::to_os_path treats backslashes as directory separators. Attackers can supply object keys such as /..\bucket2\secret to bypass the traversal check and read or modify files in other buckets.

SurrealDB 3.0.4 before 4.0.0 does not apply operator-configured WebSocket frame, message, and buffer size limits to the GraphQL WebSocket upgrade handler at GET /graphql, falling back to permissive library defaults. Unauthenticated remote attackers who supply the target namespace and database in request headers can hold up to 64 MiB of in-flight data per concurrent connection, exhausting server memory and degrading availability.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. Unauthenticated attackers can resend such an array just within the 30-second socket idle timeout to hold connections open indefinitely and exhaust RedisNetworkExecutor threads.

actix-http 3.0.0 before 3.20.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to exhaust memory by sending large-window brotli request bodies. Attackers can send an 850-byte body with Content-Encoding: br declaring a 2^30 window, forcing about 1 GiB of decoder allocation per request and OOM-killing servers.

actix-files before 0.7.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read hidden files by requesting Windows 8.3 short-name aliases. Attackers can request short names like ENV~1 or GIT~1/config to bypass the leading-dot check in actix_files::Files and retrieve .env secrets and .git contents.

pypdf 3.7.1 before 7.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows attackers to guess placeholders in encrypted templated documents by analyzing file identifiers. Attackers with a document sharing the same template and access to other documents' file identifiers can recover placeholder contents from encrypted PDFs.

pypdf before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to cause large memory usage by supplying crafted PDF cross-reference streams. Attackers can craft a PDF whose cross-reference stream offsets all point to one large object, exhausting memory in applications parsing the file.

pypdf 2.4.2 before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its handling of XFA forms that allows attackers to cause excessive memory consumption. Attackers can supply a crafted PDF containing XFA forms with many small fields so that loading the forms consumes large amounts of memory, causing a denial of service.

Hysteria from 2.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains an ACL bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to reach blocked UDP destinations by reusing an established UDP session. Attackers can open a session to an allowed destination, then send later packets to localhost or private-network addresses to access internal-only UDP services.

Hysteria 2.5.0 before 2.9.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the HTTP sniff implementation that fails to limit header size. Attackers can continuously send excessively large HTTP headers without terminating them, exhausting server memory and causing out-of-memory crashes.

Web-Token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.10, 4.0.0 before 4.0.7, and 4.1.0 before 4.1.7 contain an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability in PBES2AESKW::unwrapKey(), which passes the attacker-controlled p2c JWE header value to hash_pbkdf2() without an upper bound. Unauthenticated attackers can send a JWE using a PBES2-HS*+A*KW algorithm with a huge p2c iteration count to force lengthy PBKDF2 computations and exhaust server CPU.

Bio-Formats versions before 8.5.0 contain an XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerability in the Leica Microsystems metadata parsing component (e.g., XLEF). The parser uses an insecurely configured DocumentBuilderFactory when processing Leica XML-based metadata files, allowing external entity expansion and external DTD loading. A crafted metadata file can trigger outbound network requests (SSRF), access local system resources where readable, or cause a denial of service during XML parsing.

A flaw was found in xdgmime. A heap-based buffer overflow can be triggered in _xdg_mime_magic_parse_magic_line() in the xdgmimemagic.c file on little-endian systems when an attacker-controlled MIME magic file in a user-writable XDG data location (e.g., in the $XDG_DATA_HOME/mime/magic path) is parsed by an application performing MIME type detection (e.g., via g_content_type_guess()). When performing byte-swap, incorrect pointer arithmetic on the write side causes an out-of-bounds write of 2 bytes, resulting in an application crash or memory corruption.

A vulnerability was found in RPM's rpmbuild tarball processing. When processing a crafted source archive, the getTarSpec() function in tools/rpmbuild.cc passes an attacker-controlled tar archive member name to rpmExpand() as part of a %{basename:...} macro expression. A specially crafted .spec member name can therefore inject RPM macros, including Lua expressions, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running rpmbuild. This can be exploited when a victim or automated build system processes an attacker-controlled source tarball using rpmbuild tarball mode (such as -ts, -ta, or -tb).

A flaw was found in rpm. A local attacker could supply a specially crafted `.gem` filename containing RPM macro syntax. When a user or automated workflow invokes `rpmuncompress -x` on this file, the macro expansion occurs during command construction. This allows the attacker to execute arbitrary commands with the privileges of the invoking account, leading to a compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

A stack out-of-bounds write vulnerability was found in gfs2-utils. In gfs2_edit, the di_height field from on-disk inode metadata is used as an array index without bounds checking, causing a stack buffer overflow that may lead to arbitrary code execution when processing crafted GFS2 filesystem images.

A stack out-of-bounds write vulnerability was found in gfs2-utils. In savemeta, the height value from on-disk inode metadata is used as a loop bound without bounds checking, causing a stack buffer overflow that may lead to arbitrary code execution when processing crafted GFS2 filesystem images.

Nango through 0.72.6 fails to validate caller-supplied connection configuration values interpolated into provider token and proxy URL templates. Authenticated attackers can supply malicious configuration values to direct server requests at internal addresses or cloud metadata endpoints (0.71.3 and later block cloud metadata and loopback addresses by default but still permit private network addresses), potentially exfiltrating provider credentials.

A path traversal vulnerability in Flatpak's handling of the export/bin directory during app deployment allows a malicious Flatpak app to cause deletion of attacker-chosen files outside the deployment directory when the app is installed or upgraded. In system-wide installations, the deletion is performed as root.

A path traversal vulnerability in Flatpak's handling of the files/etc directory during app deployment allows a malicious Flatpak app to cause certain host system files (such as passwd, group, machine-id, or resolv.conf) to be emptied or replaced with a symlink when the app is installed or upgraded. In system-wide installations, the write is performed as root.

A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. Parsing a symlink entry in an untrusted RPM package whose declared RPMTAG_LONGFILESIZES value is 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF causes an integer overflow in iterReadArchiveNext() that shrinks a buffer allocation to one byte, after which the payload's independently-controlled cpio filesize field is used to write attacker-controlled data past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an  untrusted package.

A heap-based buffer overflow flaw was found in rpm. RPMTAG_FILESIGNATURES in a crafted, unsigned RPM package's main header is declared with the wrong header type, causing hex2binv() to allocate a one-byte buffer and then write the tag's attacker-controlled, hex-decoded content — of attacker-chosen length — past the end of that allocation. This is reachable via rpm2cpio, rpm2archive, and rpm -qlvp on an untrusted package.

NLTK before 3.10.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in WekaClassifier that allows attackers to bypass nltk.pathsec containment by supplying unvalidated model paths. Attackers controlling the model_filename or model argument can make the weka JVM write files via -d or probe files via -l outside allowed data roots.
Untrusted pointer dereference in SysInternals allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

OpenEMR before 8.3.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in the Standard REST API patient insurance and employer search, which concatenates query-string parameter names into SQL as column identifiers without escaping. A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer. When an application processes a crafted MXF file, an off-by-one bounds check can allow a one-byte write past the logical end of a temporal offset array. OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in patient_tracker_status.php that allows low-privilege authenticated users to modify other patients' tracker entries by supplying arbitrary tracker_id values. Attackers can post statustype and roomnum parameters with a valid CSRF token to alter patient-flow status, room assignments, and linked calendar appointment state.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

libceph: bound mon_command ack decode to front len

handle_command_ack() bounds the decode with msg->front_alloc_len, the size
of the reply buffer, instead of msg->front.iov_len, the number of bytes the
monitor sent.  mon_alloc_msg() routes every CEPH_MSG_MON_COMMAND_ACK to
get_generic_reply(), which returns the preallocated ->reply of whichever
generic request carries the same tid, so the buffer keeps its fixed size
however short the reply is.  An ack with hdr.front_len below sizeof(struct
ceph_mon_request_header) + sizeof(u32), including 0, still passes
ceph_decode_need(), and ceph_decode_32() returns four bytes that were never
received: uninitialized slab memory, stale bytes of an earlier message, or
bytes the peer planted by sending a reply that lands in the same buffer and
is then rejected.  The read stays within the allocation, so KASAN does not
flag it.

req->result reaches userspace through ceph_monc_do_statfs(),
ceph_monc_get_version() and ceph_monc_blocklist_add(); rbd hands it back
from write() on /sys/bus/rbd/add_single_major, and rbd_get_client() passes
it to ERR_PTR() unchecked, which faults:

  rbd: failed to get latest osdmap: -186318427
  BUG: unable to handle page fault for address: fffffbfffe9ca034
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
  RIP: 0010:do_rbd_add (drivers/block/rbd.c:7105)
  Call Trace:
   ...
   kernfs_fop_write_iter (fs/kernfs/file.c:345)
   vfs_write (fs/read_write.c:595 fs/read_write.c:687)
   ksys_write (fs/read_write.c:739)
   do_syscall_64 (arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:61 arch/x86/entry/syscall_64.c:84)
   entry_SYSCALL_64_after_hwframe (arch/x86/entry/entry_64.S:121)
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception

Use msg->front.iov_len, matching handle_subscribe_ack(),
handle_statfs_reply(), handle_get_version_reply() and handle_auth_reply().
A well-formed ack has front.iov_len >= 22 and is unaffected; a short one
takes the existing bad: path.  This applies commit d3c32939fa0e ("libceph:
bound get_version reply decode to front len") to the last decode-side
use of front_alloc_len in this file.

Flowise through 3.1.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal services by exploiting unpinned DNS validation in checkDenyList(). Attackers can configure a chatflow with Playwright or Puppeteer loaders using a DNS-rebinding domain so headless Chromium fetches internal or cloud metadata endpoints, returning responses as document content.

Race condition in CredentialProvider in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a local attacker to potentially execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a local program. (Chromium security severity: Medium)

Buffer overflow in CrashReporting in Google Chrome on on Windows prior to 158.0.8127.36 allowed a local attacker who had compromised the renderer process to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox via a local program. (Chromium security severity: High)

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usx2y: Initialize idle URBs before submitting streams

usb_stream_start() submits the first two capture and playback URBs and
only afterwards assigns sk->idle_inurb, sk->idle_outurb,
sk->completed_inurb and sk->completed_outurb to the remaining two URBs
of each direction.

A transfer can complete as soon as usb_submit_urb() has been called, so
the completion handler i_capture_start() or i_playback_start() may run
before those pointers are set.  While the stream is still being
synchronized (state below usb_stream_sync1), stream_start() then calls
playback_prep_freqn(sk, sk->idle_outurb) with sk->idle_outurb still
NULL, and the packet descriptors are written through that NULL pointer:

  Oops: general protection fault, probably for non-canonical address
  0xdffffc0000000018: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN
  KASAN: null-ptr-deref in range [0x00000000000000c0-0x00000000000000c7]
  RIP: 0010:playback_prep_freqn+0x11c/0x4a0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:33
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   stream_start+0x5dc/0x8d0 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:596
   i_capture_start+0x3da/0x710 sound/usb/usx2y/usb_stream.c:654
   __usb_hcd_giveback_urb+0x238/0x550 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1657
   usb_giveback_urb_bh+0x20b/0x530 drivers/usb/core/hcd.c:1691
   tasklet_hi_action+0xa/0x20 kernel/softirq.c:994
   handle_softirqs+0x16f/0x440 kernel/softirq.c:645
   </IRQ>

The four URBs referenced by these pointers are allocated long before and
do not depend on any transfer state, so assign them before the submit
loop.  Keeping the assignment inside the retry path also restores a
well-defined URB rotation when the start frame mismatch handling kills
and resubmits the streams.

NocoDB from 0.301.4 before 2026.10.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated workspace viewers to read pending invitation tokens through the workspace member list. Attackers can redeem an exposed higher-privileged invitation token at signup to claim the invited account and escalate to roles such as workspace owner.

Incus before 7.6.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows clients with project event-view access to read migration websocket secrets broadcast in operation metadata. Attackers can connect to in-flight migration control and fs websockets before the legitimate peer, hijacking the transfer to obtain instance configuration and filesystem data.

Chamilo LMS is an open-source learning management system. Prior to 1.11.40 and 2.0.1, main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php and public/main/lp/lp_ajax_save_objectives.php trust the request uid parameter instead of the authenticated user identity when saving SCORM learning objectives. Any authenticated student can replace uid with another user's identifier and overwrite that user's objectives because the endpoint performs no ownership check. This issue is fixed in versions 1.11.40 and 2.0.1.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command Execution and Launch of Phishing Attacks.

keystore-go is a Go implementation of the Java KeyStore encoder and decoder. In 2.1.0 and earlier, keystore.Decode in decoder.go does not check the error returned when reading the trailing SHA-1 integrity digest and bounds its comparison by the length of the digest actually read. If an attacker with write access removes the final 20-byte digest from a modified JKS file, the empty actual digest causes the comparison loop to execute zero times and Decode returns the parsed keystore without an error. For certificate-only stores using TrustedCertificateEntry values, this bypasses both tamper detection and password verification, allowing trusted CA certificates to be added or replaced without knowing the keystore password and potentially enabling interception or modification of TLS connections that trust the forged CA. This issue is fixed in version 3.0.0.

Mareforma is a local verification layer for AI-assisted research. From 0.3.0 until 0.3.7, the _maybe_update_replicated_unlocked convergence path in mareforma/db/core.py uses generated_by labels without requiring a valid signature_bundle from a distinct enrolled signer, so an unsigned claim written to a shared graph can converge with a signed peer and be promoted to REPLICATED. The forged trust state is returned by queries requiring REPLICATED support, allowing false multi-party endorsement signals to reach downstream consumers. This issue is fixed in version 0.3.7.

Attendize through 2.8.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in EventOrdersController::postCancelOrder() that allows authenticated organisers to cancel attendees belonging to other accounts' events. Attackers can cancel one of their own orders while supplying foreign attendee IDs, which Attendee::findFromSelection() loads unfiltered, invalidating tickets for any event on the installation.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc()

rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to
l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release
the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale.

The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting
and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Its RCU read-side critical
section starts after l3mdev_ip6_out(), so it cannot prevent the old route
from being reclaimed in between.

Reload the route from the current skb destination after
l3mdev_ip6_out() returns.

KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route
allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and
the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. This vulnerability allows for information disclosure when performing offline scans of untrusted filesystem images, such as container images or virtual machine (VM) disks. Because the scanner does not properly restrict symbolic link (symlink) resolution to the target image's root directory, an attacker can supply a crafted image containing links pointing to files on the host system. When the scan runs, typically with elevated privileges, OpenSCAP follows these links to read sensitive host files and expose their contents in the scan report or manipulate compliance results.

VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against the wrong buffer. Local attackers can place a symlink with a long target on a disc path a user opens to overflow resolved_path[] and link[], crashing the process or potentially executing code if mitigations are bypassed.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 to 3.10.3, NLTK ZIP package extraction can write through an existing in-root hardlink whose other link points outside the NLTK data root. A local attacker who can prepare the extraction target can cause a package member write to overwrite an out-of-root file, violating the pathsec containment boundary and affecting integrity and availability. This issues is fixed in version 3.10.4.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through saved search dispatch and access stored credentials and indexed data or modify lookup data.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied saved search dispatch values before it places the values into an SPL search.
For more information see Search endpoint descriptions (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/leverage-rest-apis/rest-api-reference/10.4/search-endpoints/search-endpoint-descriptions) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could use Data Model Acceleration to run malicious Search Processing Language (SPL) commands and perform actions through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API that the user cannot perform directly.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize user-provided data before it adds that data to a generated search.
For more information, see Accelerate data models (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.2/use-data-summaries-to-accelerate-searches/accelerate-data-models), Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities), and About the search language (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.6/search-overview/about-the-search-language).

In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, an unauthenticated user could craft a malicious link that, if opened by an authenticated user, executes arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with the victim's permissions. 
Successful exploitation could allow the unauthenticated user to access or modify data, alter Splunk platform configurations, and disrupt operations available to the affected user.
The vulnerability is possible because the Portable Document Format (PDF) generation component processes request data before it rejects deprecated GET requests and does not apply SPL safeguards for risky commands to subsearches.
For more information see Generate PDFs of your reports and dashboards (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/create-dashboards-and-reports/reporting-manual/10.4/report-management/generate-pdfs-of-your-reports-and-dashboards) and SPL safeguards for risky commands (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/best-practices-for-splunk-platform-security/spl-safeguards-for-risky-commands) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user that holds a role with the mc_view_im_data capability could cause the Mission Control incident mapping Representational State Transfer (REST) API to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) commands with elevated permissions. With this access, the user could expose all data in Splunk indexes and all stored credentials and modify protected indexes and lookup data.
The vulnerability is possible because the Mission Control incident mapping REST API does not validate incident identifiers before including them in SPL searches.
For more information see Capability reference for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/capability-reference-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Overview of Mission Control in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/user-guide/8.7/mission-control/overview-of-mission-control-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with edit permission for the container label of a pending external prompt could obtain the external prompt link through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API and use the link to view and resolve the associated approval.
The vulnerability is possible because the approval detail REST API includes the external prompt link in responses outside the assigned approval scope.
For more information see REST Approval (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/6.3.1/approval-endpoints/rest-approval), REST External Prompt (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/rest-api-reference/7.1.0/external-prompt-endpoints/rest-external-prompt), and Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.5.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user who can view and edit containers in at least one container label could create artifacts with parent relationships to containers and artifacts outside those labels. This could expose fields from restricted artifacts and modify incident lineage.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify access to the selected parent container and parent artifact when it creates an artifact.
